topics.label: Introduction to complement and its importance
topics.groupedBecause: This opening welcomes students to the lecture and frames complement as an important, complicated subject.

topics.label: Complement activation, immune defence and clearance functions
topics.groupedBecause: This overview explains the basic stages of complement activation and the ways complement contributes to immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature and its exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions for complement components and the exceptions that make them confusing.

topics.label: C3-centered complement activation and recognition pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how C3 serves as the central point of complement activation and how recognition pathways build surface-bound C3b to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated complement produces downstream immune effects that help respond to pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and protection of host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins limit complement activation on the body's own cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic relates deficiencies in complement components and regulators to their distinct clinical consequences.

topics.label: Staphylococcus aureus complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how Staphylococcus aureus evades complement and how its protein A is used to handle antibodies in clinical and laboratory settings.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture, thanks the audience, and points to the next lecture.
